EXPLORATORY RESEARCH PROTOTYPE

Seeing the physical–virtual relationship

This viewer displays recorded data, not a simulated reconstruction of the control mechanism. Overview trajectories are resampled to 10 Hz. Invalid samples and gaps are not joined. Raw-frame positions anchor event markers. High-frequency coordination measures should be calculated from the original recordings.

Comparison and coordinates

Shared-scene coordinates preserve target layout. Head alignment translates each run by its initial head X/Z position; it does not rotate to head yaw. Floor height is retained. External views share a camera and scale. First-person mode follows each panel’s own recorded head position and orientation, including roll, with a 0–15 cm forward offset (default 3 cm). The schematic 85° vertical field of view is not calibrated to headset optics. Poses use the nearest 10Hz overview sample. Missing poses produce a blank panel. The current head marker and rays are hidden. This analytical view does not reconstruct the original rendered headset image. Playback aligns elapsed countdown time, not matched target actions. Front/rear/side presets are fixed scene views; they do not follow current head rotation. Standard camera presets enable repeatable views; orthographic projection removes perspective size differences.

Head orientation and left/right

The cyan arrow shows headset forward, not eye gaze. The blue/orange crossbar indicates headset left/right; the short grey line shows up, making roll visible. Optional history rays occur every two seconds. All directions come from recorded headset quaternions, converted as vectors into the viewer coordinates. Raw Unreal quaternions are not applied directly as Three.js quaternions.

Blue/orange always refer to recorded left/right channels, regardless of screen position. A face-on Front view puts the participant’s left on the screen’s right; Rear looks forward from behind. Side views can occlude or visually reverse paths. The channel audit compares physical and virtual pair directions and projects hand separation on the headset’s horizontal right axis; it does not establish dominant handedness or rule out source-side anatomical labelling errors.

What the colours mean

Blue is left; orange is right. Solid paths are physical, dashed paths virtual. Event and target spheres are schematic markers, not the true collision geometry. Density counts hand sample time in 10 cm voxels, with one common colour scale across A and B. Group density sums time across all main runs in a condition; it is not normalised per person. Selection frequency counts unique participants in main runs only, not stated preference.

Interpretation limits

Early-release flags and goal attribution remain provisional. Unattributed terminal outcomes are not confirmed misses; some counter increments are compatible with repeat scoring. Ownership, agency and workload are global participant responses, not ratings of each condition. No per-condition subjective effect is implied.

Reusable modules

The versioned JSON separates tracks, targets, events and textual annotations. Compatible modules can add events with a position, time, evidence label and text. Downloaded JSON includes the coordinate convention and camera metadata. The VRChat bridge contains a Unity editor importer and notes; it is a starting point, not a tested VRChat world.

Physical trajectory visibility

Physical paths use opaque, adjustable screen-space strokes (3px by default), rather than one-pixel native WebGL lines. By default they are drawn in the foreground so other layers cannot hide them. Turn off “Keep physical trails visible through layers” for depth occlusion. This affects visibility, not recorded coordinates; stroke width is not limb size. Virtual paths remain thin and dashed.

Time series and 3D encodings

Distances are from the head to each hand (solid physical, dashed virtual). Activity is world-space physical speed in cm/s, derived from 10Hz overview positions and averaged causally across three samples; it is not the earlier TI measure or a measure of effort. A common vertical scale is used for A and B. Optional physical-hand brightness encodes 0–100cm/s, clipped at 100; hand hue remains left/right. Virtual halos encode actual factor 0–0.65 on a shared scale. Summaries are descriptive and computed for the displayed time window. These display measures do not replace raw-resolution analyses.

Next-target prediction

The backtest predicts the next new target attachment at fixed horizons using available targets, virtual-hand approach and headset direction/turning. Features use only samples at or before the cutoff, with 0.3s trailing history. Forecasts require no currently attached target. Availability excludes previously attached targets and targets that descended below a 20cm floor proxy since their latest reset; displacement alone does not make a target unavailable. Combined weights are selected using other participants’ main runs only (leave-one-participant-out). Favourite runs are excluded from primary evaluation. The continuous ranking overlay is exploratory: event-aligned accuracy does not establish continuous false-positive rates or intended targets on failed attempts.
